/-!
# Finitely presented periodic groups

A group is *periodic* (or a *torsion group*) if every element has finite order. No uniform
bound on the orders is assumed. A group is *finitely presented* if it has a presentation
$\langle S \mid R \rangle$ with a finite set of generators $S$ and a finite set of relators $R$.

The general Burnside problem asked whether every finitely generated periodic group is finite.
Golod and Shafarevich answered it negatively in 1964. It is open whether the answer becomes
positive when "finitely generated" is strengthened to "finitely presented".

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Group_theory)
- [Wikipedia, Presentation of a group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/finitely_presented_group)
- [Wikipedia, Burnside problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside_problem)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Group.FG` (finitely generated only; too weak, since the general Burnside problem for finitely generated groups is solved negatively), `PresentedGroup` (a construction, not a predicate on groups), `Module.FinitePresentation`/`Algebra.FinitePresentation` (module/algebra analogues, not applicable to groups), and `Group.fg_iff_exists_freeGroup_hom_surjective` (only gives finite generation).
justification.name: FinitelyPresented.IsFinitelyPresented
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has `PresentedGroup rels` (a concrete quotient of a free group) and `Group.FG`, but no predicate saying that an abstract group admits a finite presentation. The conjecture quantifies over all finitely presented groups, so such a predicate is required.

/-- A group `G` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for some
finite type of generators `α` and some finite set of relators `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=

    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (α : Type) [Finite α] :
    IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup α) := by
  have h : Subgroup.normalClosure (∅ : Set (FreeGroup α)) = ⊥ :=
    le_bot_iff.mp <| Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _)

/--
Is every finitely presented periodic group finite?

That is, if a group $G$ has a finite presentation $\langle S \mid R \rangle$ and every element
of $G$ has finite order (with no uniform bound on the orders assumed), must $G$ be finite?
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (a Burnside-type problem): the Prop is `∀ G, (G finitely presented) → Monoid.IsTorsion G → Finite G`; 'periodic' means every element has finite order with no uniform exponent assumed (unbounded, so this is distinct from the bounded Burnside problem), and Mathlib lacks a finitely-presented-group predicate so one must be introduced (e.g. isomorphism to `PresentedGroup rels` over a `Finite` generator type with `rels` a `Set.Finite`).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful Prop: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G → Monoid.IsTorsion G → Finite G, with Monoid.IsTorsion = every element has finite order (no uniform exponent) and a bespoke IsFinitelyPresented = isomorphic to PresentedGroup rels over a finite generator type with rels.Finite. They differ only in mathematically equivalent encodings (Fin n vs. arbitrary Finite α; G : Type vs Type*; direction of ≃*). c01 chosen because its generator encoding (arbitrary Finite type) matches the informal definition most directly, it uses G : Type* like ErdosProblems/274.lean, and it ships the most complete set of proven API/test lemmas for the bespoke definition (presentedGroup is f.p., invariance under ≃*, f.p. ⇒ Group.FG, free group on finite type is f.p.), as CONTRIBUTING requests for bespoke definitions. Only edit: copyright year 2025 → 2026 to match the checkout's majority/latest commit date. Compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Finitely presented periodic groups

A group is *periodic* (or a *torsion group*) if every element has finite order. No uniform
bound on the orders is assumed. A group is *finitely presented* if it has a presentation
$\langle S \mid R \rangle$ with a finite set of generators $S$ and a finite set of relators $R$.

The general Burnside problem asked whether every finitely generated periodic group is finite.
Golod and Shafarevich answered it negatively in 1964. It is open whether the answer becomes
positive when "finitely generated" is strengthened to "finitely presented".

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Group_theory)
- [Wikipedia, Presentation of a group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/finitely_presented_group)
- [Wikipedia, Burnside problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside_problem)
-/

namespace FinitelyPresented

/-- A group `G` is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to `PresentedGroup rels` for some
finite type of generators `α` and some finite set of relators `rels : Set (FreeGroup α)`. -/
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)),
    rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)

/-- A group presented by finitely many generators and finitely many relators is finitely
presented. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup {α : Type} [Finite α] {rels : Set (FreeGroup α)}
    (hrels : rels.Finite) : IsFinitelyPresented (PresentedGroup rels) :=
  ⟨α, inferInstance, rels, hrels, ⟨MulEquiv.refl _⟩⟩

/-- Being finitely presented is invariant under group isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv {G H : Type*} [Group G] [Group H]
    (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) (e : G ≃* H) : IsFinitelyPresented H := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα, rels, hrels, ⟨f⟩⟩ := hG
  exact ⟨α, hα, rels, hrels, ⟨f.trans e⟩⟩

/-- A finitely presented group is finitely generated. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsFinitelyPresented.fg {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsFinitelyPresented G) :
    Group.FG G := by
  obtain ⟨α, hα, rels, -, ⟨e⟩⟩ := hG
  have : Group.FG (PresentedGroup rels) :=
    Group.fg_iff.mpr ⟨Set.range PresentedGroup.of, PresentedGroup.closure_range_of rels,
      Set.finite_range _⟩
  exact Group.fg_of_surjective (f := e.toMonoidHom) e.surjective

/-- The free group on a finite type is finitely presented (with no relators). -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup (α : Type) [Finite α] :
    IsFinitelyPresented (FreeGroup α) := by
  have h : Subgroup.normalClosure (∅ : Set (FreeGroup α)) = ⊥ :=
    le_bot_iff.mp <| Subgroup.normalClosure_le_normal (Set.empty_subset _)
  exact (isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup Set.finite_empty).of_mulEquiv
    ((QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq h).trans QuotientGroup.quotientBot)

/--
Is every finitely presented periodic group finite?

That is, if a group $G$ has a finite presentation $\langle S \mid R \rangle$ and every element
of $G$ has finite order (with no uniform bound on the orders assumed), must $G$ be finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem finitely_presented :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G], IsFinitelyPresented G → Monoid.IsTorsion G →
      Finite G := by
  sorry

end FinitelyPresented

items: 'Periodic' is formalized as `Monoid.IsTorsion G` (every element has finite order) with no uniform bound on orders, as the list entry and the Burnside-problem article intend; this is deliberately different from the bounded Burnside problem (`∀ g, g^n = 1` for a fixed n) already in `BoundedBurnsideProblem.lean`.

'Finitely presented' is formalized by the new predicate `IsFinitelyPresented G := ∃ (α : Type) (_ : Finite α) (rels : Set (FreeGroup α)), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (PresentedGroup rels ≃* G)`. The generator type lives in `Type` (universe 0) while `G : Type*`; this loses no generality since any finite generating set can be re-indexed by `Fin n`, and `MulEquiv` works across universes.

The question is stated with `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` per CONTRIBUTING.md; `answer(True)` means every finitely presented periodic group is finite, `answer(False)` means an infinite finitely presented periodic group exists.

The group is quantified as `G : Type*` (universe-polymorphic), matching e.g. `ErdosProblems/274.lean`, rather than `Type` as in `BoundedBurnsideProblem.lean`; the truth value does not depend on the universe since finitely presented groups are countable.

The bespoke definition was placed in the problem file (not `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`) because the task restricts output to the single candidate file; a reviewer may prefer moving `IsFinitelyPresented` and its API lemmas to `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/GroupTheory/`.

Extra declarations are all `@[category API]`/`@[category test]` with complete proofs: `isFinitelyPresented_presentedGroup`, `IsFinitelyPresented.of_mulEquiv`, `IsFinitelyPresented.fg` (finitely presented ⇒ `Group.FG`), and `isFinitelyPresented_freeGroup` (free group on a finite type is finitely presented). The (true) fact that every finite group is finitely presented was not included because its proof is not short.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot and no omission reasons to weigh. Verified: Monoid.IsTorsion G := ∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g (periodic, unbounded); Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no finitely-presented-group predicate, so a bespoke one is necessary. Boundary cases benign: hypotheses are satisfiable (e.g. trivial group via α = Empty, rels = ∅; all finite groups are finitely presented), so the implication is not vacuous; answer(True) is the positive answer and answer(False) asserts an infinite finitely presented periodic group exists. Universe choice (Type*) is harmless since finitely presented groups are countable and all predicates transfer along isomorphisms. Reviewer note: the bespoke definition IsFinitelyPresented and its API lemmas live in the problem file because the pipeline outputs a single file; a maintainer may prefer moving them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/GroupTheory/ (e.g. as Group.IsFinitelyPresented) and adding the file to the FormalConjecturesForMathlib.lean index.
